title: The representing object of a truncated simplicial object is the limit over the truncated simplex category
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file simplicial.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-formula-limit at source lines 2553-2570: for an n-truncated simplicial object U of a category C and the contravariant functor sending T to the set of (n+2)-tuples of maps T -> U_n satisfying the n+1 simplicial identities, if that functor is representable then its representing object is the limit of U over the opposite of the truncated simplex category over [n+1]. The proof at source lines 2572-2642 is a substantial comparison of two descriptions of the same functor. It must first write the limit as the set of compatible families indexed by the maps [k] -> [n+1] with k <= n, then construct maps from a representing object to that limit and back, and finally check compatibility. The constructive part is the interesting half: an element of the limit gives a family, and the proof has to manufacture, out of the family and a chosen representing tuple, the value at the extra index [n+1] -> [n+1] and then verify the simplicial identities by a factorisation argument through a chosen simplex map, computing U(psi) applied to the value at an index as the value at the composite index. The statement records none of the indexing bookkeeping. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
